title: Session boundary contracts: JIT provisioning, MFA expectations, logout propagation, and grace handling
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem summary: We continue to see edge cases where user sessions created via Just-In-Time (JIT) SAML provisioning have inconsistent security posture compared to long-lived accounts. Symptoms include: stale or 'orphaned' sessions after IdP-initiated logout, confusion about whether MFA asserted at provisioning must be rechecked for sensitive actions, and delayed RBAC v2 enforcement when admin role changes occur. Admins also report incomplete audit entries when logout or forced reauth events occur. This ticket defines a session boundary contract, reconciliation behavior, and enforcement points to make session lifecycle predictable and auditable across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Define a session token contract that includes source, idp_assertion_id, saml_session_index, provision_time, role_version, and revocation_id.
New sessions created via JIT must encode whether MFA was asserted by the IdP and the acr value; step-up is required for high-risk actions when assertion is absent or stale.
Implement back-channel logout handling and a revocation list with propagation to runtime within SLA (<60s for Dedicated, <120s for Hosted under normal conditions).
Periodic reconciliation job to detect orphaned accounts/sessions created by JIT and mark them disabled after configurable grace (default 30 days) if IdP no longer returns subject or mapped groups.

Audit log events emitted for: provision, login, logout (front and back channel), force-logout, reauth step-up, role_version bump. Each event includes idp_assertion_id, admin_actor (if applicable), and correlation_id.
RBAC v2 enforcement: role changes bump role_version and trigger 'session_enforcement' events; runtime will reject or require reauth for mismatched sessions per policy.
End-to-end tests and canary rollout completed with no more than 0.1% increase in authentication latency and no dropped active sessions during controlled rollouts.
technical_notes: Token contract: add 'src' (saml|oauth|local), 'idp_assertion_id', 'saml_session_index', 'provision_ts', 'role_version', 'revocation_id'. Store minimal session metadata in sessions store (Redis TTL aligned to token lifetime). Revocation: maintain a signed revocation list versioned by revocation_id; runtime checks revocation_id/role_version on token validation and consults cache invalidation webhook on revocation events. MFA expectations: treat 'acr' values from SAML as authoritative for a session lifetime defined in config (default 8 hours). If acr missing or < required level, mark session as 'stepup_required' for actions tagged 'high_risk' in policy store. Reconciliation: periodic job queries IdP with collected subjects and saml_session_index where available; if IdP asserts logout or no longer returns mapping, mark local account JIT:disabled and schedule forced logout after grace window. Audit: use structured logs with fields: event_type, user_id, subject, idp_assertion_id, saml_session_index, timestamp, actor, reason, correlation_id, deployment_id. Ensure these reach the audit pipeline and are available for 90 days for enterprise customers (configurable).
implementation_steps: Schema: Add fields to token payload and session store; update token issuance path in auth service (authn-team).
Runtime: Add validation hooks to check revocation_id and role_version; return explicit error code for 'reauth_required' with remediation hint.
MFA: Parse SAML 'AuthnContextClassRef' (acr) and surface acr values in session metadata; implement policy check for high-risk actions.
Logout propagation: wire IdP back-channel/logout endpoint handling and front-channel hints; on receipt, emit force-logout event and update revocation list.
Reconciliation job: implement worker to reconcile JIT accounts weekly; config for grace window and mass-disable behavior.
Audit: extend audit adapter to include new event types and ensure idp fields are captured; add test harness to validate audit entries.
RBAC v2: ensure role assignment changes increment role_version and publish session_enforcement event to the pubsub topic consumed by runtime.
End-to-end tests: unit tests for token parsing, integration tests with a SAML test IdP, and chaos test for logout propagation latency.
Canary rollout: enable for 10% of requests in staging, monitor errors and latencies, then progressively promote to 100%.
migration_plan: Phased migration: (1) Issue tokens containing role_version and revocation_id but leave runtime fallback logic to accept older tokens. (2) Start emitting audit events for provision and logout. (3) Enable runtime enforcement in a feature flag gated rollout. (4) Enable reconciliation job and automated disable after 30-day grace. Provide migration doc for Dedicated/private customers with optional configuration knobs for grace window and revocation propagation.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated deployment to auth service and runtime (start in staging).
Canary 10% traffic for 48 hours, validate metrics and logs.
Increase to 50% for 24 hours with manual verification of audit completeness.
Full rollout and enable reconciliation job with admin notifications.
Post-rollout review after 7 days to validate no regressions and collect feedback from on-call and SRE.
test_plan: Unit tests for token contract serialization/deserialization.
Integration tests: SAML IdP assert MFA/no-MFA and verify step-up behavior for high-risk API actions.
Simulate IdP-initiated back-channel logout and verify runtime rejects tokens and audit logs the event.
RBAC change test: change role in admin UI, verify role_version bump and that runtime enforces reauth where configured.
Load test: ensure auth path latency increase <0.1% p95, and revocation propagation within SLA during peak load.
Chaos test: drop pubsub messages for 30s and verify reconciliation catches any missed enforcement and does not leave sessions permanently privileged.
Manual verification checklist for Dedicated/Private deployments.
